key_insight: Combining classical coding theory with deep learning–based decoding yields a scalable, noise-tolerant pipeline for storing and reliably retrieving large amounts of data in DNA. (Note: this item is an author correction to the original paper; summary reflects the corrected framing of the work.)
problem_solved: How to make DNA data storage scalable and robust against synthesis, storage and sequencing errors so it can be practical for large-scale archival use.
method: Design of error-resilient encoding schemes from coding theory tailored to DNA constraints (GC content, homopolymers, addressability).
Deep-learning models trained to model channel noise and perform sequence-level error correction / reconstruction from noisy sequencing reads.
An integrated end-to-end pipeline that maps digital data → constrained DNA codewords → physical DNA → sequencing → DL-assisted decoding, validated across scaling scenarios.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners with a cross-disciplinary blueprint: noisy-channel modeling and learned decoders can materially improve molecular data storage systems, opening opportunities for ML-driven error correction, simulation, and optimization in wet-lab pipelines.
